request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital stay: The patient was admitted to the hospital due to the presence of a brain tumor located in the clivus region. He underwent surgical intervention via a left suboccipital craniotomy, which involved resection of the tumor. Oral intubation was done using the Macintosh laryngoscope blade, and the patient was placed in the left park bench position with neck flexion. Surgery was performed via the left lateral suboccipital approach. The lesion was decompressed, and the operation was completed successfully.

Medical Condition at Discharge: The patient had minor swelling in the neck, tongue, and pharynx on the left side. He experienced pain in the tip of his tongue with a small ulcer on the left side after returning to the intensive care unit. The swelling of his tongue gradually improved after the administration of steroids. The patient was discharged 10 days after the surgery.

Follow-Up Care: The patient was advised to undergo follow-up MRI after three months of surgery as well as clinical follow-up as per physician's recommendations.

Discharge Medications: None.

Instructions: The patient was advised to follow-up with his physician for regular check-up and take rest until complete recovery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: C41**

The discharge summary withholds the final diagnosis, so this is inferred. A tumour of the clivus, the bone at the base of the skull, is most often a chordoma, which is a malignant bone neoplasm classified under C41 (C41.0 covers bones of the skull and face). If histology showed a different tumour, such as a meningioma, the category would change. The tongue and pharyngeal swelling and the tongue ulcer were post-operative complications and do not alter the principal diagnosis.
